![What's new in Hamstr 0.7.3](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Mailo037/Hamstr/v0.7.3/docs/images/releases/v0.7.3.png)

Hamstr 0.7.3 replaces the Windows installer and lets the desktop app install its own updates.

- **A quick setup for Windows.** The setup no longer goes through Windows Installer (MSI). It installs Hamstr for you into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Hamstr` in a few seconds: no administrator prompt, no long wait before it, and no restart, neither to install nor to remove it. A running Hamstr is closed first, the tray included, which is what made removing the old one ask for a restart.
- **From 0.7.0–0.7.2:** run the new setup once (or update from inside Hamstr). It removes the old Hamstr that was installed for all users; Windows asks for permission one last time for that. Your settings and downloads stay.
- **Updates install themselves.** *Update* in Settings › About downloads the new version, checks it, closes Hamstr, installs it in the background and opens Hamstr again. The portable zip updates its own folder; on macOS the app is replaced from the `.dmg`, on Linux the `.deb` installs after your password.
- **No detour to GitHub.** While a release's installer for your system is still being built, Hamstr says it's on its way and looks again every few minutes. Running in the tray, it checks every few hours instead of only at start.
- **Quit means quit.** Hamstr's process ends completely, so no file stays in use.

Signed APKs are available for arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a, x86_64 and all ABIs together. The desktop installers aren't signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen and macOS Gatekeeper ask before the first start. Verify every file against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
